findings.title: Violet / indigo gradient
findings.why: The purple-to-blue gradient is the most recognisable AI-product colour move.
findings.fix: Replace with one flat brand colour. If depth is needed, use a surface step and a 1 px line, not a gradient.

findings.title: Page scrolls sideways
findings.why: Horizontal overflow is a bug, most often on phones.
findings.fix: Find the widest element, give it max-width: 100% or let it wrap; do not hide the overflow on body.

findings.title: Text below WCAG contrast
findings.why: Grey-on-tint and pale-on-white text fails readers and audits alike.
findings.fix: Darken the text (or lighten the surface) until body text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1.

findings.title: Stock framework palette
findings.why: Untouched indigo/violet/slate swatches from popular utility palettes make unrelated products look alike.
findings.fix: Derive the palette from the brand: one accent chosen on purpose, neutrals tinted toward it.

findings.title: Stock marketing vocabulary
findings.why: Words such as "seamless", "elevate" or "unleash" carry no information and mark the text as generated.
findings.fix: Say the concrete thing: what the product does, for whom, with what number or example.

findings.title: Emoji in the page
findings.why: Emoji in headings, buttons, labels or body copy are the most visible AI tell.
findings.fix: Remove them. Use words, or one icon set drawn for the product. Keep emoji only if the brief says the user asked for them (<meta name="unslop-brief" content="emoji: reason">).

findings.title: Faded support text
findings.why: Light grey support text that passes the bare minimum still reads as faded; it is the "muted subtitle" look of generated pages and tires the eye.
findings.fix: Readable text at 7:1 or more (4.5:1 from 24 px up). Rank with size and weight, not by greying text out.

findings.title: Emoji used as interface icons
findings.why: Emoji in headings, buttons and list items render differently per platform and signal a quick draft.
findings.fix: Use one consistent line-icon set (one size, one stroke width) or remove the glyph.

findings.title: Heading plus grey subtitle, section after section
findings.why: A heading followed by a smaller, greyed paragraph in every section is the template rhythm of generated landing pages.
findings.fix: Let the section open with its content (a product view, a table, a list) or write one sentence in the main text colour. Vary how sections start.

examples.detail: "Unleash seamless workflows. N…" with a greyed subtitle
"Secure by design" with a greyed subtitle

findings.title: Icon in a rounded coloured tile, repeated
findings.why: A tinted square with a glyph above a heading is the default feature-card opener.
findings.fix: Drop the tile. Use a bare icon at one size, or no icon and let the heading carry the card.

findings.title: Eyebrow label above the heading
findings.why: A small, spaced, uppercase tag above every heading is a template habit.
findings.fix: Delete it, or fold the information into the heading. Keep at most one, and only if it carries a fact.

findings.title: Coloured stripe down one side of a box
findings.why: A thick left border on a card, alert or quote is a common AI shortcut for emphasis.
findings.fix: Emphasise with a tinted surface, a heading or an icon. Do not use a one-sided accent border.

findings.title: Text glued to the screen edge
findings.why: Copy that starts within 8 px of the viewport edge has no page margin.
findings.fix: Give the page container a side padding of at least 16 px on phones and 24 px on desktop.

findings.title: Social proof with no source
findings.why: Round user counts, star scores and "trusted by" lines that cannot be checked read as invented.
findings.fix: Cite the source and date, link to the real logo or review, or delete the claim.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text
findings.why: Headings or numbers clipped to a colour ramp are a stock "AI landing" signature.
findings.fix: Set the text in one solid colour; emphasise with size, weight or position instead.

findings.title: Coloured glow shadow
findings.why: Large zero-offset shadows in a saturated colour fake "energy" and hurt legibility.
findings.fix: Use a neutral, low-alpha shadow with a real offset, or no shadow and a 1 px border.

findings.title: "Not X, but Y" headline formula
findings.why: Defining the product by what it is not ("not just a tool, it's a partner") is a reflex of generated copy.
findings.fix: State the claim directly: say what it is and what the reader gets.

examples.detail: Unleash . Not just a tool, it's a partner.

findings.title: Row of identical icon + title + text cards
findings.why: Three or four same-size feature cards in a row say nothing about which point matters.
findings.fix: Rank the points: one larger block for the main idea, the rest as a list or table.

findings.title: Pulsing status dot
findings.why: A blinking "live" dot on a status that never changes pretends the product is alive.
findings.fix: Show status only when it comes from data, as text plus colour, without animation.

findings.title: Announcement pill above the hero heading
findings.why: A rounded "New: ..." badge above the h1 is on nearly every generated landing page.
findings.fix: Remove it. If there is real news, link it in the header or footer.

findings.title: Blurred colour blob behind the content
findings.why: Soft coloured orbs in the hero background are decoration without subject.
findings.fix: Remove the blob. If the hero needs an image, use a real photo, product screen or diagram.

findings.title: Overlapping avatar row
findings.why: A stack of round faces beside "trusted by" is the stock proof device, and the faces are rarely real.
findings.fix: Replace with a named customer quote that can be checked, or remove.

findings.title: Ornament that animates forever
findings.why: Endless loops (floating shapes, shimmering text, tickers) compete with content and drain batteries.
findings.fix: Animate in response to an action and then stop. Keep infinite loops for real loading indicators only.

findings.title: Stock fake names and data
findings.why: Acme, Globex, John Doe and "User 1" are the placeholder cast of generated demos.
findings.fix: Use plausible, specific sample entries, and label them as sample data.

examples.detail: "Fluxly changed how we work." — Jane Do…

findings.title: One word of the headline in the accent colour
findings.why: Colouring or gradient-filling one keyword of the headline is the most common template tell, even on design-tool sites.
findings.fix: Let the whole headline speak in one colour. If a second tone is wanted, make it a quieter grey for a whole line, not a bright keyword.

examples.detail: "seamless workflows" coloured inside "Unleash seamless workflows. Not just a …"

findings.title: AI-default font
findings.why: Display serifs and text faces that agents pick by reflex (the list in references/ai-default-fonts.md) make every generated page sound the same.
findings.fix: Choose a face for this project and write why in the brief. To keep a listed face on purpose, add <meta name="unslop-brief" content="font: Family, reason">.

findings.title: Focus outline removed without a replacement
findings.why: Keyboard users cannot see where they are.
findings.fix: Add :focus-visible with a 2 px outline (or ring) in an accent colour; never leave outline: none alone.

findings.title: Padding and gaps ignore a 4 px rhythm
findings.why: Values like 13, 18 or 22 px show that spacing was typed, not chosen from a scale.
findings.fix: Pick a 4 px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64) and snap every padding and gap to the nearest step.

findings.title: Heavy weights carry the hierarchy
findings.why: Weights of 800 to 900, or bold on most text, flatten emphasis. Hierarchy should come from size and colour.
findings.fix: Use 400 and 500 (600 sparingly). Let size and tone do the ranking.

findings.title: Arrow glyph on many links
findings.why: Appending "→" to every link and button is decoration.
findings.fix: Keep an arrow only on the single primary action, if direction carries meaning.

findings.title: Everything fades up on load or scroll
findings.why: Six or more elements entering with the same fade-and-rise turns motion into wallpaper.
findings.fix: Animate one moment (the hero, or one key reveal). Leave the rest still.

findings.title: Several text elements under 13 px
findings.why: Three or more small text elements make a page tiring to read, especially on phones.
findings.fix: Raise captions and labels to at least 13 px (body 16 px).

findings.title: Accent colour spent on decoration
findings.why: When the accent paints rules, tags and ornaments, it no longer tells the reader what to press or what changed.
findings.fix: Keep the accent for actions, selection, focus, live state and the key data series. Decoration goes neutral.

findings.title: Frosted glass on several surfaces
findings.why: Backdrop blur on many elements costs performance and rarely has anything meaningful behind it.
findings.fix: Use solid surfaces. Keep blur for at most one overlay that really sits over content.

findings.title: Heavy resting shadows
findings.why: Large dark shadows on elements at rest make the page look puffy and dated.
findings.fix: Keep shadows only on floating layers (menus, dialogs) and make them subtle: low alpha, small blur.

findings.title: Decorative section numbers
findings.why: "01 / 02 / 03" on content that has no sequence is ornament.
findings.fix: Number only real steps (use an ordered list). Otherwise drop the numbers.

findings.title: Border, soft shadow and tint on every card
findings.why: Stacking a border, a diffuse shadow and a different fill on the same surface is three signals for one idea.
findings.fix: Pick one separator per surface: a border, or a tint, or (for floating layers only) a shadow.

findings.title: Touch targets under 32 px
findings.why: Small buttons and links are hard to hit on a phone.
findings.fix: Make every control at least 44 px tall (minimum 32 px) with padding rather than larger text.

findings.title: Body text set too tight
findings.why: Multi-line paragraphs under 1.3 line-height, or letter-spacing below -0.04em, are hard to read.
findings.fix: Body line-height 1.5 to 1.7; keep tight leading for headings only and never track tighter than -0.03em.

findings.title: Text sits against the edge of its box
findings.why: Buttons and cards with almost no inner padding read as unfinished.
findings.fix: Give buttons at least 12 px horizontal and 8 px vertical padding (anything under 8 px horizontal is flagged), cards at least 16 px.

findings.title: Cards lift or grow on hover
findings.why: translateY(-4px) and scale(1.05) on hover is a stock micro-interaction.
findings.fix: Change tone or border colour on hover, only inside @media (hover: hover).

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion handling
findings.why: People who ask the system for less motion still get all of it.
findings.fix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that removes or shortens animations and transitions.

findings.title: transition: all
findings.why: Animating every property triggers layout work and surprising effects.
findings.fix: List the properties you mean (opacity, transform, background-color) with a duration and easing.

focal.why: headline 3.7x, largest visual 0% of the screen

visual.why: 0% of the first screen is visual (none)

motion.why: moves outside any visual, 15 moving elements, reduced motion not handled

identity.why: no web font, one face, accent used 26x in 5 hue band(s), 4 shadows, 1 layers, 1 textured areas (gradient)

density.why: landing, 25% of the first screen holds content

findings.title: No real visual on the first screen
findings.why: A first screen of text alone asks the reader to imagine the product. Strong pages show it: a product view, a photo, a drawing.
findings.fix: Put the product itself in the first screen: a built UI view, a real screenshot, a photo or a meaningful drawing, at least 8% of the screen.
